0.0.n: Here it opens the presentation rather than answering a question.

0.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

0.4.n: Part of the English channel name, not a separate Japanese word.

0.6.n: The final English word in the channel name.

0.7.n: This borrowed word identifies the type of media account.

0.8.n: Links the channel to its presenter, showing affiliation.

0.9.n: This is the name portion of the handle Haru99, not the ordinary meaning spring.

0.10.n: These digits are part of the presenter's handle Haru99.

0.11.n: A polite ending used to introduce oneself; the speaker leaves I unstated.

1.0.n: Sets the time of the introduction without needing a particle.

1.1.n: ご adds respectfulness to 紹介する, which comes before アイテム to describe it.

1.2.n: A borrowed word for the product being presented.

1.3.n: Marks the item as what the speaker is talking about.

1.4.n: A polite way to point out the item being shown.

2.0.n: A company name referring here to the game's Japanese publisher.

2.1.n: Attached to the company name to show friendly respect; it is not limited to people's names.

2.2.n: Identifies Tendays as the company that performed the localization.

2.3.n: With ね, this creates a conversational pause rather than a separate statement.

2.4.n: Part of ですね, keeping the listener engaged during a pause.

2.6.n: 日本語版 means Japanese edition; 化 adds the sense of turning something into that form.

2.7.n: Polite past of される, used here as a respectful form of する for the publisher's action.

2.9.n: The first part of the game's title, Glass Road.

2.10.n: The second part of the game's title, Glass Road.

2.12.n: Politely identifies the item as Glass Road.

2.13.n: Softens the identification and invites the listener to follow along.

3.0.n: Refers back to the Japanese edition of Glass Road.

3.1.n: Marks the game as the thing that has come out.

3.2.n: A conversational filler that gives the speaker a brief pause.

3.4.n: Suggests the release came after some waiting.

3.5.n: Polite past of 出る; for products, coming out means becoming available.

3.6.n: Works with the following で as ので, introducing the reason for the next action.

3.7.n: Completes ので; it is not the separate particle used for locations or tools.

3.8.n: After ので, this adds conversational politeness rather than changing the reason clause.

3.9.n: Completes the filler ですね while the speaker prepares to continue.

4.0.n: Sets the time frame for the planned review.

4.1.n: Marks today as the time frame the speaker wants to focus on.

4.2.n: Presents the unboxing as the first planned activity.

4.3.n: Refers to the game being shown.

4.4.n: Links the game to its unboxing review.

4.5.n: Means opening a sealed package and combines with レビュー to name the review type.

4.6.n: A borrowed word used with 開封 for a review centered on opening the product.

4.7.n: Marks the unboxing review as what the speaker wants to deliver.

4.8.n: お届けする is a humble way to describe delivering something to the audience.

4.9.n: The たい form of する expresses desire and completes お届けしたい.

4.10.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

4.11.n: Polite form of 思う; after たいと, it makes the speaker's intention sound softer.

0.lit: Yes, I am The Game Gallery channel's Haru99.
0.tip: Channel name + の + personal name introduces someone affiliated with that channel.

1.lit: The item I introduce today, as for it, this one.
1.tip: ご紹介する comes before アイテム, so it describes the item being introduced.

2.lit: Tendays respectfully made a Japanese edition of Glass Road; it is that, you see.
2.tip: されました is respectful here, not passive: が marks Tendays as the company doing the localization.

3.lit: This, well, finally came out, so, you see,
3.tip: ので connects the release to the speaker's next action by giving a reason.

4.lit: Today, first, I think I want to bring you an unboxing review of this.
4.tip: たいと思います is a soft, polite way to announce what you would like to do.
